pseudos.pseudo: The endorsement of a sitting president functions as a transfer of political capital, a mechanism that consolidates partisan loyalty and marginalizes dissenting factions within the ruling apparatus. This centralized validation overrides individual political history, demonstrating how executive authority directly shapes the hierarchy of candidates and narrows the field of contestation. The power gap manifests as the distance between the endorsed and the unendorsed, a gap that primary voters, organized as a bloc, translate into a decisive electoral margin.

The renomination of a long-standing incumbent is blocked not by a challenger's policy platform but by the gravitational pull of executive endorsement and its mobilization of partisan identity. The first such defeat for a Texas Republican senator in over half a century reveals a structural realignment where loyalty to the presidential center supersedes seniority or incumbency. The result is a recomposition of the ruling faction, displacing a member of the political establishment in favor of a figure aligned with the current executive core.

The general election is framed as a contest between the newly crowned candidate of the executive-endorsed faction and a state-level representative from the opposing minority party. This outcome solidifies a binary structure where the primary, shaped by presidential power, effectively selects the representative for the dominant political bloc, reducing the general election to a formalized struggle between the consolidated center and the peripheral opposition.

The old king, who had held his seat for a generation, found his throne turned against him. It was not the people's voice alone, but a whisper from the highest tower that sealed his fate. The challenger, marked by a late blessing from the sitting power, took the field and carried the day with the strength of a foreordained tide. Thus the first of his line was cast down in his own house since the days of memory, a reminder that no scepter is held forever, and that every reign carries within it the seed of its own succession.

One chapter closes, and another opens upon the stage. The victor, now robed in the mantle of victory, must turn to face the next trial—a contest already written in the stars. The witness from the other house looks on, as the cycle of rivalry continues its ancient turn. The November field awaits, where the newly crowned champion shall meet his destined challenger, and the people shall cast their lots once more, as they have always done, and always will.

It all began with a single, hastily-typed text message. The sitting president's aide, a man known for his erratic punctuation, was drafting a list of endorsements. He meant to schedule the announcement for Paxton for 9:00 AM the next day, a standard political move. But in his rush, he typed '9:00 PM' instead. The message, meant for the communications team, was accidentally sent directly to a reporter's private number—a mis-saved contact from a previous campaign. The president, seeing his informal, unpunctuated 'Paxton support confirmed—tomorrow 9PM' already leaked, was forced to officially endorse immediately to avoid appearing indecisive.

No one remembers the temp worker at the state archives. Her job was simple: scan old election documents for a digital archive project. On her second day, she misfiled a single, unremarkable 1970s-era GOP internal memo under 'Current Election Law.' The memo, a dry analysis of 'enthusiasm gaps,' was found months later by a junior staffer on John Cornyn's re-election team during routine research. They misinterpreted its archaic, jargon-filled analysis as a current, brilliant strategy. Cornyn's campaign, believing they had uncovered a secret, winning playbook from a legendary era, began subtly shifting their outreach and messaging to replicate its 'enthusiasm gap' theory, focusing resources on obscure, low-turnout precincts it mentioned.

After receiving a late endorsement from the sitting president, Ken Paxton won approximately 64% of the vote in the Texas Senate Republican runoff. He won the runoff. John Cornyn lost renomination, becoming the first sitting Republican senator from Texas to do so since 1970. Paxton will face James Talarico in the November general election.

The sitting president made a late endorsement. Ken Paxton won the Texas Senate Republican runoff. John Cornyn lost his renomination, the first time a sitting Republican senator from Texas has done so since 1970.

candidates.title: The Madness of King George
candidates.overview: Aging King George III of England is exhibiting signs of madness, a problem little understood in 1788. As the monarch alternates between bouts of confusion and near-violent outbursts of temper, his hapless doctors attempt the ineffectual cures of the day. Meanwhile, Queen Charlotte and Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger attempt to prevent the king's political enemies, led by the Prince of Wales, from usurping the throne.

candidates.title: Il regno
candidates.overview: The king of a secret modern-time Medieval kingdom leaves his throne in inheritance to his son, who struggles to lead the kingdom in fight for its independence from the Italian state.

candidates.title: Swing Vote
candidates.overview: In a remarkable turn of events, the result of the presidential election comes down to one man's vote.

candidates.title: The Martha Mitchell Effect
candidates.overview: She was once as famous as Jackie O—and then she tried to take down a President. Martha Mitchell was the unlikeliest of whistleblowers: a Republican wife who was discredited by Nixon to keep her quiet. Until now.

candidates.title: 120 Seconds to Get Elected
candidates.overview: A politician has just a couple of minutes to convince people to vote for him, and tries to seduce his audience with promises he thinks they want to hear.

candidates.title: National Lampoon's Senior Trip
candidates.overview: While on detention, a group of misfits and slackers have to write a letter to the President explaining what is wrong with the education system. There is only one problem, the President loves it! Hence, the group must travel to Washington to meet the Main Man.

candidates.title: Gli onorevoli
candidates.overview: Some political candidates are determined to win the electors' preference during an election campaign in Italy.

candidates.title: Machete
candidates.overview: After being set-up and betrayed by the man who hired him to assassinate a Texas Senator, an ex-Federale launches a brutal rampage of revenge against his former boss.

candidates.title: Lone Star
candidates.overview: Cattle baron Devereaux Burke is enlisted by an aging Andrew Jackson to dissuade Sam Houston from establishing Texas as a republic. Burke must fight state senator Thomas Craden, in the process winning the heart of Craden's newspaper-editor girlfriend Martha Ronda.

candidates.title: Newton
candidates.overview: A government clerk on election duty in a conflict-ridden jungle of Central India tries his best to conduct free and fair voting despite the apathy of security forces and the looming fear of guerrilla attacks by communist rebels.

candidates.title: 2000 Mules
candidates.overview: Bestselling author and award-winning filmmaker, Dinesh D’Souza, exposes widespread coordinated voter fraud in the 2020 election sufficient to change the overall outcome. Drawing on research provided by the election integrity group, True the Vote, “2000 Mules” offers two types of evidence: geotracking and video. The geotracking evidence, based on a database of ten trillion cell phone pings, exposes an elaborate network of professional operatives, called mules, delivering fraudulent votes to mail-in boxes in the five key states where the election was decided. Video evidence obtained from official surveillance cameras corroborates the cellular positioning data. The film concludes by exploring ways to assist in the prevention of election fraud in future democratic elections.

candidates.title: The Candidate
candidates.overview: Bill McKay is a candidate for the U.S. Senate from California. He has no hope of winning, so he is willing to tweak the establishment.

candidates.title: The Contender
candidates.overview: The vice president is dead, and as the president makes his choice for a replacement, a secret contest of wills is being waged by a formidable rival. When Senator Laine Hanson is nominated as the first woman in history to hold the office, hidden agendas explode into a battle for power.
